source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:23 ('written גיים, read גוים — and every nations-word in the Torah is plene vav with one yod EXCEPT THIS, written with two yods and no vav; so our rabbis expounded: it is written GEYIM' — Avodah Zarah 11a, Bereshit Rabbah, Shochar Tov 9)
claim_en: THE TWO PROUD ONES IN THE WOMB: שני גיים ('TWO NATIONS are in your womb') — the Torah's ONE nations-word written with two yods and no vav (the qere reads גוים): SNAPSHOT carries the written and the read side by side (two-token encoding), and the census locks the rule — bare plene גוים stands 18 times, the lean two-yod form ONCE, here. The Talmud's derash rides the ktiv: read it GEYIM, the two lordly ones — Rebbi and Antoninus at one table (Avodah Zarah 11a).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:23 (the plene control)
claim_en: ...the plene control censused: bare גוים with the vav — eighteen tokens across the Torah, the qere-token of this verse among them.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:23 ('יעבד defective — and EVERY serve-verb of this form in the Torah likewise'; Bereshit Rabbah 63 via the Yefeh Toar: 'if worthy — he SHALL BE SERVED; if not — he shall SERVE': the reading rides the lean spelling)
claim_en: THE TWO-WAY SERVE-VERB: ורב יעבד צעיר ('and the elder shall serve the younger' — or the reverse) — written DEFECTIVE, no vav, and Bereshit Rabbah 63 makes the ambiguity explicit: the lean verb can be read active or passive, 'if worthy... if not' — the oracle's double edge lives in the missing letter. Census: the form stands SIX times in the Torah, all defective (no plene token exists, builder-asserted): the oracle shares its lean verb with the service-laws — the Hebrew slave (Exod 21:2), the jubilee hireling (Lev 25:40), the Levite's retirement (Num 8:25-26), the unworked valley (Deut 21:4).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:25 ('אדמוני plene in all precise books and the Hilleli; the Masorah: TWO, and plene — its fellow is David's'; the Ramah concurs)
claim_en: THE TWO RUDDY ONES: אדמוני ('and the first came out RUDDY') — UNIQUE in the Torah, written plene as all the precise books rule; the Masorah's pair-leg is David (I Sam 16:12, 17:42; edges): Esau and David share the red — the midrash's contrast (one sheds blood by whim, one by the Sanhedrin's word) hangs on the pair.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:25 (the plene leg)
Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:24 ('תומם — lacking yod and aleph: the eleven she was worthy to bear, per the midrash')
claim_en: THE LEAN TWINS AND THE FULL: תומם ('behold, TWINS in her womb,' 25:24) — written doubly lean (no aleph, no yod), unique in the Torah; and its one full counterpart is Tamar's תאומים ('twins,' Gen 38:27) — the tradition's contrast letter-exact on SNAPSHOT: Rebecca's twins (one wicked) written lean, Tamar's twins (both righteous) written whole.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:24 (the full counterpart)
claim_en: ...the full twin-word censused: תאומים stands once — Tamar's verse alone.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:21 ('הוא is written — teaching that BOTH were barren,' Yevamot 64); Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 25:21
claim_en: THE BOTH-BARREN SKELETON: כי עקרה הוא ('for she was barren') — the she-word written in the masculine skeleton הוא carrying the feminine vowel (the pentateuchal written-he), and Yevamot 64 rides exactly that: read the consonants — HE; read the vowels — SHE: 'both were barren, and he was entreated FOR HIM.' SNAPSHOT: the pointed masculine skeleton stands.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:21 ('ויעתר — the tav in SEGOL')
claim_en: ...and the answer-verb ויעתר ('and YHWH WAS ENTREATED of him' — the passive, 25:21's second entreat-token) carries the tav in segol as ruled: the prayer goes out in patach, the answer returns in segol — one verse, one verb, two stems pointed apart.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:22 ('ויתרצצו — the tzadi with sheva ALONE, per our custom')
claim_en: DISCREPANCY, FOURTH STATION OF THE HALF-VOWEL SPLIT: ויתרצצו ('and the children STRUGGLED within her') — Minchat Shai rules the tzadi with plain sheva; SNAPSHOT points HATAF PATACH (the compound half-vowel): the sheva-vs-hataf codex split (the bless-word class: 12:3, 22:18, 24:60) now reaches the twins' first struggle. Watchlist.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:22 ('למה זה — the zayin DAGESHED; so its two fellows')
claim_en: למה זה ('WHY THEN am I thus?') — the zayin dageshed as ruled (with its two fellow dotted zayins in the tradition's list). Rebecca's question carries the pressed letter.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:32 ('ולמה זה — two in the Masorah WITH maqqef; the other: why then vain breath' — the despiser walked after vanity)
claim_en: ולמה־זה ('behold, I go to die — WHY THEN a birthright to me?') — joined by maqqef, machine-checked by column; the Masorah's maqqef-pair leg is the vain-breath verse (Job 27:12; edge): the Kitzur reads Esau's why into the breath he chased.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:23 ('מלאם — the lamed SOFT with the mem, against the custom of its fellows; the Michlol, page 51')
claim_en: ולאם מלאם ('and one PEOPLE shall be stronger THAN THE OTHER') — the lamed of מלאם soft (no dagesh) against the doubling custom, exactly the Michlol's noted exception; and both people-words written lean of vav as the earlier ruling records. SNAPSHOT: soft and lean.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:27 ('איש תם — the final letters: SHEM, for he sat in the tents of Shem')
claim_en: SHEM IN THE FINALS: איש תם ('Jacob was a WHOLESOME MAN, dwelling in tents') — the pair closes ש-ם: the letters of שם ('Shem'), in order — the Kitzur reads the tent-sitter's teacher sealed in the phrase's ends.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:30 ('הלעיטני נא מן — the initials: HAMAN; as Jacob bought from Esau with bread and lentils, so Mordechai bought Haman for bread')
claim_en: HAMAN IN THE GULP: הלעיטני נא מן ('POUR INTO ME, please, from this red-red stuff') — the three words open ה-נ-מ, the letters of המן ('Haman'): the Kitzur reads Esau's descendant sold-for-bread already in the wolfed-down stew.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:20 ('לבן הארמי — the letters of THE DECEIVER')
claim_en: THE ARAMEAN IS THE DECEIVER: הארמי ('Laban THE ARAMEAN') — the gentilic's five letters are exactly the letters of הרמאי ('the deceiver'), the Kitzur's anagram: the letter spells the character into the nationality. Multiset-verified at Laban's token.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:20 ('בקחתו — two in the Masorah: at his TAKING Rebecca, and the bound-in-chains taking of Jeremiah: as the one there was bound, so here — Isaac too was bound in barrenness'; the Manoach parallel drawn)
claim_en: בקחתו ('at his TAKING of Rebecca') — UNIQUE in the Torah; the Masorah's pair-leg is Jeremiah taken bound in chains (Jer 40:1; edge): the Kitzur reads Isaac's own boundness (the barren years) into the shared taking-word.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:26 ('וידו — three in the Masorah: his hand grasping the heel; His outstretched hand; His hand divided it by line — at his birth the hint that the nations fall into his hand')
claim_en: וידו ('AND HIS HAND grasping Esau's heel') — UNIQUE in the Torah; the Masorah's legs are the outstretched hand over the nations (Isa 14:26-27) and the hand that divided the land by line (Isa 34:17; edges): the birth-grip read forward into the fall of the nations.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 25:34 ('ויבז — two: Esau despised; and he despised to lay hands on Mordechai alone — the despiser son of the despiser')
claim_en: ויבז ('and Esau DESPISED the birthright') — UNIQUE in the Torah; the Masorah's pair-leg is Haman's despising (Esth 3:6; edge): 'the despiser son of the despiser' — the verb passes from ancestor to heir across the canon.
